sections.title: Campaign Overview
sections.content: May 2026 was a month defined by access and timing challenges more than outright rejection. A significant proportion of conversations ended not because prospects were opposed to Jiminny, but because the moment simply wasn't right — people were between roles, unwell, heading into meetings, travelling, or on leave. The market felt busy and somewhat distracted, and this flavour of resistance was consistent across the board. Where genuine conversations did take place, the responses were largely civil and considered, suggesting that awareness of Jiminny as a brand is present in the market, even if that didn't translate into pipeline this month.
sections.content2: The clearest competitive pattern to emerge was the entrenchment of Gong. Multiple prospects referenced it unprompted, not as something they were evaluating but as something they were doubling down on — expanding contracts, integrating it more deeply with their existing stack. This represents a more stubborn barrier than simple incumbent inertia; these are prospects who are actively reinvesting. Alongside this, a recurring structural objection surfaced: a meaningful number of companies pointed to large internal sales enablement or revenue operations teams as the reason Jiminny's proposition wasn't relevant, suggesting that in certain organisational profiles, the problem Jiminny solves is being handled in-house.
sections.content3: On a more positive note, the data quality and targeting picture is worth addressing directly. Several calls landed on entirely wrong contacts — freelancers, people who had already left their roles, or individuals with no sales team to speak of. Refining the contact list would likely have a material impact on the quality of conversations in the months ahead. The three activations achieved this month, while modest, came from conversations where genuine curiosity was present, and the pipeline of follow-ups — people who asked to be called back at a later date — represents a tangible base to work from going into June.

rows.what_said: Multiple prospects mentioned Gong as their current solution, with at least two explicitly noting they were expanding their contract rather than considering alternatives. One prospect said they are 'already sorted with Gong and expanding their contract.'
One prospect mentioned they are using Outreach as part of their current sales tech stack, indicating a decision-maker for this area sits in the US rather than locally.

Several prospects cited large, dedicated internal teams as the reason external solutions were unnecessary. One said they have 'a large internal sales enablement team handling coaching and forecasting.'
Mentioned by one prospect in passing as a tool they were already aware of, referenced positively in the context of declining Jiminny's proposition.

items.quote: They are already sorted with Gong and expanding their contract.
items.analysis: This is the most commercially significant objection of the month. Prospects are not just sitting with existing tools — they are actively renewing and expanding them, which narrows the window for displacement. Messaging that speaks directly to what Jiminny offers that Gong does not, particularly around ease of use, pricing, or specific features, would help create a reason to at least have the conversation.

items.objection: Not the right time or bad timing
items.quote: He mentioned he isn't available at the moment. He asked me to call back next week.
items.analysis: A high volume of conversations were cut short by timing rather than genuine disinterest. This is a positive signal in the sense that prospects were not hostile, but it does suggest the follow-up cadence needs to be robust. Every 'call me back' commitment should be treated as a warm lead and actioned promptly.

items.quote: They are currently in a cost-cutting phase and not interested in new investments.
items.analysis: Budget constraints are surfacing in a small but notable number of accounts. This objection is worth monitoring — if it increases in frequency over coming months, it may reflect broader market conditions. For now, it is worth having a value-led response prepared that speaks to ROI and efficiency gains rather than leading with product features.

items.objection: Team too small or solution not relevant
items.quote: Call recording analysis isn't relevant for them due to their manageable size of six sales reps.
items.analysis: Several prospects self-disqualified on the basis of team size, suggesting that either targeting is pulling in companies below the ideal customer profile threshold, or that there is a perception issue around minimum viable team size. Tightening the target list to organisations with larger sales functions would reduce this friction.

items.objection: Decision sits elsewhere (wrong contact or geography)
items.quote: I need to reach someone in the US for further discussions.
items.analysis: A recurring pattern of being directed to head offices, US-based decision-makers, or revenue operations leads suggests that the contact data may not always be mapping to the right level of seniority or the right geography. Where referrals to specific individuals or departments are given, these should be actively pursued as they represent a warmer route in than a cold dial.

items.quote: They have a large internal sales enablement team handling coaching and forecasting, so it's not relevant for her.
items.analysis: Where companies have invested in building internal capability, they are unlikely to be receptive to an external platform unless there is a clear gap in what their team delivers. Messaging for this persona might focus on how Jiminny complements rather than replaces internal functions, or on the scalability and consistency benefits that even well-resourced teams struggle to maintain manually.

items.question: Can you call back at a better time?
items.analysis: The frequency of this soft deflection indicates that prospects are not immediately dismissive but are genuinely pressed for time. This is an invitation rather than a rejection, and following up with discipline on each of these instances could convert a proportion of them into conversations with a warmer starting point.

items.question: Who should you actually be speaking to?
items.analysis: Multiple prospects redirected calls to other individuals or departments, suggesting that contact mapping needs refinement. However, each redirect is also a small piece of organisational intelligence — understanding who owns the sales technology decision in each account is valuable even when the current contact is not the right person.

items.heading: Gong entrenchment is the primary competitive barrier
items.body: Across several accounts, Gong was not simply in place but actively being expanded and deepened. This goes beyond standard incumbent resistance — these companies are doubling down on their existing investment, which makes a near-term switch unlikely. The practical implication is that Gong accounts may need a longer nurture cycle, with outreach timed around renewal windows rather than cold introductions.

items.heading: Organisational complexity is routing decisions away from frontline contacts
items.body: A consistent pattern this month involved being redirected to US head offices, revenue operations functions, or senior leaders in other geographies. This suggests that sales technology decisions are increasingly centralised and that reaching the right stakeholder requires more precise targeting at the outset. Where referrals to specific individuals were given, these should be followed up as high-priority leads.

items.heading: Team size and relevance perception is filtering out smaller accounts
items.body: Several prospects disqualified themselves on the basis that their team was too small to benefit from Jiminny's proposition. Whether or not this is accurate, the perception is real and is causing early exits from conversations. Reviewing the minimum team size threshold in the target criteria, and considering whether messaging needs to address smaller teams differently, would help reduce this form of self-disqualification.

items.heading: A notable portion of non-conversions were circumstantial rather than commercial
items.body: Transitions between roles, illness, parental leave, and mid-travel encounters accounted for a meaningful share of conversations that went nowhere this month. These are not lost accounts — they are deferred conversations, and a structured follow-up approach timed appropriately could reactivate a good number of them over the next one to two months.

items.heading: Data quality is reducing the effective reach of the campaign
items.body: Several dials landed on entirely wrong contacts — a self-employed lawyer, a person who had already left the business, and existing customers who were inadvertently included. Each misdirected call represents not just a wasted dial but a potential reputational risk if the same contacts are reached repeatedly. A data audit ahead of June would likely improve both efficiency and the quality of first impressions.

sections.title: Recommended Actions
items: Conduct a data quality audit on the contact list before June — remove confirmed leavers, existing customers, and contacts below the ideal company size threshold to reduce wasted dials and improve the signal-to-noise ratio in conversations.

Build a structured follow-up sequence for all 'call me back' and 'not now' outcomes from May — including Roger (settling into new VP of Sales role), Tom (recovering from illness), Laura (end-of-year budget review), Joe (six to eight months), and Melvin (requested callback next week) — as these represent the warmest near-term opportunities.

Develop a specific response to the Gong objection that does not attempt to displace it head-on, but instead identifies a gap or complementary use case — prospects who are expanding Gong contracts are unlikely to switch, but may be open to a conversation framed around what Gong does not cover.

Pursue the referrals received during May as priority outbound targets: John Healy in the UK (referred by Alex), the revenue operations lead at Doxel (referred by a RevOps-adjacent contact), and Mark (referred by Jamie who agreed to pass along information directly).

Review the targeting criteria to ensure contact records map to individuals with direct ownership of sales technology or coaching decisions — the volume of redirections to US offices and revenue operations functions suggests that current contacts are often one or two steps removed from the actual decision-maker.

Jamie indicated that the BDR function is shrinking at their company, but he thinks Mark is looking into similar solutions. He agreed to pass my information to Mark and will facilitate a conversation after I send him details later today. I'll follow up later this week.

Joe suggested I check back in six to eight months for any changes. He indicated that it probably wouldn't be of interest for now, given their current situation.

conversationSummaries.signalReason: Satisfied with Gong but offered a six-to-eight-month revisit window

conversationSummaries.jobTitle: Sales Director - Europe & Director Partner Development EMEA @ Laserfiche | Strategic Partnerships
conversationSummaries.notes: Spoke with a leader from a very small sales team of two reps. They mentioned that my solution is probably not relevant for them at this time. I acknowledged their team size and recognized that I might be wasting their time. No further steps were discussed.

conversationSummaries.notes: Called John at a smaller sales team. He indicated that call recording analysis isn't relevant for them due to their manageable size of six sales reps. They have no plans to scale or hire at the moment. I thanked him for his time and left the conversation open for potential future relevance.
conversationSummaries.summary: John at Ravelin leads a six-person international sales team and doesn't see call recording analysis as relevant at that size. There are no plans to scale or hire, removing a key trigger for future relevance. The conversation closed with no follow-up planned.
conversationSummaries.signalReason: Small team with no growth plans makes solution irrelevant

conversationSummaries.notes: I reached out to Stephen, but he indicated that our services weren't relevant to his team as they already focus heavily on training and coaching, mitigating issues with call slips. He asked to have his number removed, and I explained how to opt-out. He appreciated the recommendation for the tool "Surf" and thanked me before ending the call.
conversationSummaries.summary: Stephen at GlobalData stated that his team's existing focus on training and coaching already addresses the pain points Jiminny targets. He requested his number be removed from contact lists, signalling a hard stop. The call ended after an opt-out discussion.
conversationSummaries.signalReason: Requested number removal indicating firm disengagement

conversationSummaries.notes: I reached out to Charlie for a cold call. He expressed that they are not interested in our services and mentioned they don't need any of the tools we offer. No specific objections were noted, but he appreciated the call. No next steps were discussed.
conversationSummaries.summary: Charlie Walker at Ravelin declined interest on a cold call with no specific objections raised. He stated the tools offered aren't needed, and no further conversation was pursued. The rejection was polite but unambiguous.
conversationSummaries.signalReason: Blanket disinterest with no specific objections or openings

He mentioned that they rely on information from partners and it wouldn't be beneficial for him to pursue the solutions I offer. I acknowledged his perspective and thanked him for his time. No next steps were discussed.

conversationSummaries.signalReason: Channel-dominated model creates a structural barrier to fit

conversationSummaries.notes: Spoke with Tom, who is currently unwell. He indicated that he may be available for a follow-up call next week regarding call recording and coaching insights. I will reach out to him then, wishing him a speedy recovery.

conversationSummaries.notes: Spoke with Laura, who indicated they are currently in a cost-cutting phase and not interested in new investments. She mentioned they are not using any similar tools at the moment. Laura advised that I could check back around the end of the year for potential re-evaluation of their situation.
conversationSummaries.summary: Laura at Ion is navigating a company-wide cost-cutting phase that has put a freeze on new technology investment. She noted no similar tools are currently in use, which could signal future opportunity, and suggested revisiting at year-end. The timing is the primary blocker rather than a lack of fit.

conversationSummaries.notes: I spoke with Roger, who mentioned he's currently in between positions and won't be able to focus on our discussion until he lands a new role as VP of Sales in Europe. He suggested I follow up in a month when he's settled. He's interested but can't engage right now due to ongoing interviews.

He expressed genuine interest in the conversation but is unable to engage meaningfully until he is settled in a new position. He asked for a follow-up in roughly four weeks.
